hints: In $\triangle AOC$, $AO = OC = AC = r$, so the triangle is equilateral with angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Notice that in triangle $\triangle AOC$, $AO = r$ (radius of semicircle), $OC = r$ (radius of semicircle to point $C$ on the circumference), and $AC = r$ (radius of arc $OC$ centred at $A$).
Since all three sides are equal ($AO = OC = AC = r$), $\triangle AOC$ is an equilateral triangle:
$$\angle CAO = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Subtract sector area from triangle area.
walkthrough:
In right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ (with hypotenuse $AB = 2r$, side $AC = r$, and angle $\angle CAB = \frac{\pi}{3}$):
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \frac{1}{2}(AC)(AB)\sin(\angle CAB) = \frac{1}{2}(r)(2r)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = r^2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}r^2$$

Calculate the area of sector $AOC$ (centred at $A$ with radius $r$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } AOC) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}r^2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}r^2$$

Subtract the sector area from the triangle area to obtain the shaded region:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}(\triangle ABC) - \text{Area}(\text{sector } AOC) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}r^2 - \frac{\pi}{6}r^2 = r^2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6}\right)$$

ai_rubric.Area of Composite Shapes: Calculates sector area $\frac{\pi}{6}r^2$ (M1). Calculates triangle area $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}r^2$ (M1, A1). Obtains $r^2(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6})$ (A1).
